theme: Great are the works of the LORD
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 111. It is one of the alphabetic acrostic psalms, with each line beginning with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Read it as a hymn of remembering God’s works, and notice its link to the Lord’s Supper and the church’s gathering.
settingTheScene: Psalm 111 and 112 are a pair. Both begin with “Praise the LORD” and are acrostics, each with twenty-two short lines. Psalm 111 describes God and his works; Psalm 112 describes the person who fears him and reflects his character. Psalm 111 is sung in the congregation: “in the company of the upright, in the congregation.” It fits our study of the church’s worship and the meal of remembrance.
observation: “Praise the LORD! I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart, in the company of the upright, in the congregation” (v. 1).
“Great are the works of the LORD, studied by all who delight in them” (v. 2).
“Full of splendor and majesty is his work, and his righteousness endures forever” (v. 3).
“He has caused his wondrous works to be remembered; the LORD is gracious and merciful” (v. 4).
“He provides food for those who fear him; he remembers his covenant forever” (v. 5).
“He sent redemption to his people; he has commanded his covenant forever” (v. 9).
“The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; all those who practice it have a good understanding” (v. 10).
interpretation:
The psalm opens with whole-hearted thanksgiving, offered in the congregation. Worship is personal and corporate. Verse 2 says the works of the LORD are great and “studied by all who delight in them.” We are invited not only to admire God’s works but to study them. The more we look, the more we see his splendor and majesty. “His righteousness endures forever.”

Verse 4 is the heart: “He has caused his wondrous works to be remembered; the LORD is gracious and merciful.” God designs memorials. He gave Israel the Passover, the feasts, and the stones of remembrance, and he has given the church the Lord’s Supper. We tend to forget, so God gives us ways to remember. The psalm’s God is “gracious and merciful,” echoing Exodus 34:6. Verse 5: “He provides food for those who fear him; he remembers his covenant forever.” This recalls manna in the wilderness, and our daily bread. Notice that God remembers his covenant, even as he asks us to remember his works.

The next verses speak of power and justice. “He has shown his people the power of his works, in giving them the inheritance of the nations.” “The works of his hands are faithful and just; all his precepts are trustworthy; they are established forever and ever, to be performed with faithfulness and uprightness.” His commands are as reliable as his deeds.

Then the great verse: “He sent redemption to his people; he has commanded his covenant forever. Holy and awesome is his name!” Redemption is the exodus in the original context. For Christians it is also the cross, where the Lord Jesus redeemed us by his blood, establishing the new covenant. The Supper is the memorial of that redemption. And the name of the LORD is holy and awesome (the word is “fearful,” to be revered).

The psalm ends with a proverb that is also the key to the whole Bible’s wisdom literature: “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; all those who practice it have a good understanding. His praise endures forever!” Wisdom begins with reverent awe before the God who has acted. This connects with the opening chapters of 1 Corinthians, where the wisdom of God is found in the cross.
connection: Exodus 34:6-7 describes God as gracious and merciful. Exodus 12:14 and Deuteronomy 8:2 speak of remembering. Psalm 105 retells God’s works. Luke 22:19 says “Do this in remembrance of me.” Proverbs 1:7 and 9:10 say the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom. Luke 1:68 and 1:49 speak of redemption and the holy name. Revelation 15:3-4 sings “Great and amazing are your deeds.” Psalm 112 is the companion psalm. Hebrews 9:15 speaks of redemption under the new covenant.
application:
Write down three of the LORD’s works in your life and give thanks in the congregation of your family or friends.

At your next Communion, pray verse 4: he has caused his wondrous works to be remembered.

Study one of God’s works this week, in creation or in Scripture, and delight in it.
prayerPrompts: Give thanks to God with your whole heart.
Tell him about works of his that you want to remember.
Ask him to give you the fear of the LORD that is the beginning of wisdom.
